Finding: Section renders a snippet name that does not exist
Detail: Line 38 calls {% render 'social-micro-post-card' %}. The file on disk is q-social-micro-post-card.liquid. sections/social-media-micro-post-strip.liquid calls the same snippet with the correct q- prefix, so this is a half-completed rename.
Evidence: Renderer aborts on this section with a lookup failure; theme-wide scan confirms the un-prefixed name exists nowhere.
Consequence: The section cannot render at all. This is why it reported that no configuration renders a block.
Recommended fix: Change the reference to 'q-social-micro-post-card'.
Phase 3 notes: Absent in the approved post-Phase-2 source; no Phase-3 deletion.

Finding: The calendar can never display an event, from any data source
Detail: The section accumulates its event list with `assign raw_pairs = raw_pairs | push: pair` at lines 63, 116 and 186 -- once in each data-source branch. `push` is not a Shopify Liquid filter. Shopify returns nil for an unknown filter, so raw_pairs becomes nil on the first iteration, sorted_pairs is nil, has_events computes 0, and the render loop at line 267 iterates nothing.
Evidence: Rendered all four source modes (blocks, metaobjects, context_metafield, feed_json). The default event title 'Open House' appears 0 times in every one. This is also why the section reported that no configuration renders a block.
Consequence: The entire section is inert for every merchant regardless of how they configure it. Nothing on the page indicates a problem.
Recommended fix: Liquid has no array-append filter. Build a delimited string with `append` and `split` it afterwards -- which the surrounding code already half does, since it constructs 'key::id' pairs and sorts them.
Phase 3 notes: Absent in the approved post-Phase-2 source; no Phase-3 deletion.

Finding: The invented `push` filter is used at 25 call sites across six files
Detail: Theme-wide count: interactive-content-pricing-data-table (18), interactive-content-helper-calendar (3), interactive-content-helper-portfolio-grid (1), main-product-simple (1), main-product-modern-variant (1), snippets/pb-bundle-card (1). `push` does not exist in Shopify Liquid and silently yields nil, destroying whatever variable it is assigned back to.
Evidence: Source scan across sections/ and snippets/. The calendar's failure (P2-15) is the proven instance; each remaining file's blast radius is confirmed as its own document is reached rather than assumed.
Consequence: Any accumulation built this way is nil. Two of the six files are main-product templates, so the product page is implicated.
Recommended fix: Replace each accumulation with an append-to-string plus split, or restructure to avoid needing an array.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: The pricing / data table renders no table at all, in any of its three modes
Detail: The section builds its column list with `assign cols = '' | split: '|'` followed by `cols = cols | push: col_N_label` (lines 251-260 and 18 call sites in total). `push` is not a Shopify filter, so cols becomes nil and every downstream size check and loop yields nothing.
Evidence: Rendered at defaults, at gates-open, and in all three modes (price_list, pricing_table, data_table). Every render produced ZERO <th> and <td> elements. 13 of the section's 17 block settings measured inert as a direct consequence.
Consequence: A merchant configures plans, columns and features and the section displays no table. This is the largest single concentration of the push fault in the theme.
Recommended fix: Same as P2-15: accumulate into a delimited string with `append` and `split` it, or restructure to avoid needing an array.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Where: the 12 content blocks in the general builder
Finding: The primitive content blocks have no styling CSS; their style controls do nothing
Detail: content-alert, content-icon-list, content-quote, content-rich-text, content-badge, content-code, content-icon, content-divider, content-spacer, content-button, content-button-group and content-heading each emit inline custom properties for colour, spacing, border, radius and typography. Nothing in the theme consumes them. A scan of every .liquid, .css and .js file for `var(--...)` finds 137 declared-but-unconsumed --qtm-* properties across 29 block files, and the concentration is total in these twelve: content-alert 17 of 17, content-icon-list 16 of 16, content-quote 15 of 15, content-rich-text 11 of 11, content-badge 11 of 11, content-code 7 of 7, content-icon 7 of 7, content-divider 5 of 5, content-spacer 3 of 3.
Evidence: Verified end to end, not by grep alone. content-alert was rendered in a full page with the theme's real stylesheets loaded (theme.css, tailwind.css, styles.css and the theme-tokens snippet), first with background and text colour red, then green. The computed styles of every element were byte-identical across the two renders, and the alert paints background-color rgba(0, 0, 0, 0), padding 0px, border-radius 0px. It is unstyled text. Composite blocks are wired by comparison: content-tabs has 2 unconsumed of 17, content-location-info 1 of 21.
Consequence: These are exactly the twelve blocks the general content builder makes available (P4-01). Every styling control a merchant touches on any of them does nothing, and an alert, badge, quote or divider renders with no visual treatment at all. Combined with P4-01, the block setter offers twelve unstyled blocks while the 49 styled ones are unreachable.
Recommended fix: Write (or restore) the stylesheet that consumes these properties, starting with q-base.css since the layout already links it. Until then no styling control on any primitive block has any effect.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Where: assets/styles.css:310 — affects every section with a checkbox or radio; measured on main-product-simple, main-product-modern-variant
Finding: The global input rule stretches every checkbox and radio in the theme, breaking the collection filters and forcing horizontal scroll on both product templates
Detail: assets/styles.css:310 declares `input, select, textarea { width:100%; min-height:44px; padding:.7rem .85rem; border:1px solid; border-radius; background; color }` with no `:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio])` exclusion. Every one of the theme's 90 checkbox/radio inputs (51 checkboxes, 39 radios) inherits a full-width, 44px-tall, bordered, opaque box. On main-product-simple and main-product-modern-variant the variant radios are hidden with `#MainProductModern-{id} .qtm-modern__radios input { position:absolute; opacity:0; pointer-events:none; }` (main-product-simple.liquid:355) — position and opacity only, no width, height or clip — so each radio keeps width:100% of its containing block while positioned outside the flow.
Evidence: Every checkbox and radio the theme renders was measured at 1440px across the 18 sections that contain one: 26 inputs, and all 26 carry min-height 44px from the global rule — not one escaped it, including the four that have local `width:auto` guards, because those guards do not reset min-height. The widths land wherever the flex context puts them: 0px in main-collection-classic, 1px in main-product-classic, 13px in form-waitlist, 17px in 3rd-party-bulk-ordering, 18px in product-bundles, 195px in main-collection-simple, 329px in 3rd-party-crm-lead-capture-form, and 1440px in the two product templates. Not a single one is the ~13px square a checkbox should be. For the horizontal-scroll half: at 320px the three main-product-simple radios each render 320px wide starting at x=14 (document scrollWidth 334); at 1920px they render 1920px wide with the right edge at 2956. document.scrollWidth exceeds the viewport at all five widths on both product sections. Computed style confirms position:absolute, opacity:0, visibility:visible, width:100%.
Consequence: Three separate consequences from one rule. (1) Every product page on either template scrolls sideways on every device; at desktop widths the page can be dragged roughly 1000px right into blank space. (2) No checkbox or radio in the theme renders at its intended size — see P6-13 for the worst case. (3) The symptom was already known locally: form-waitlist.liquid:102 carries the comment "avoid width:100% input styles bleeding into checks", so four sections were patched around a rule nobody went back to fix.
Recommended fix: Scope the global rule with `input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]):not([type=range])`, and give the .qtm-modern__radios hide rule a real hiding technique — `width:1px; height:1px; clip-path:inset(50%)` or `appearance:none; width:auto`. Then delete the four local guard rules, which only ever fixed half the problem.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Where: 10 files, 23 call sites — confirmed visible on main-cart, call-to-action-featured-product, main-blog-single, main-product-compact
Finding: 23 image_tag calls print the entire element on the page as escaped text
Detail: This is the severe half of the filter-in-a-named-argument fault (P2-10). Liquid does not allow a filter inside another filter's named argument, so in `| image_tag: alt: img.alt | default: title | escape` the `| escape` binds to image_tag's output, not to the alt value. Where the trailing filter is `escape`, the whole `` string is HTML-escaped and rendered as literal text. Re-counted precisely: 90 image_tag/placeholder_svg_tag sites carry a stray filter; 23 of them terminate in `escape` (visible corruption) and 67 terminate in `default` (62) or `append` (5), where only the alt attribute is silently wrong.
Evidence: Rendering with theme defaults produced escaped markup in the page body: main-cart 4 occurrences, call-to-action-featured-product 3, main-blog-single 2, main-product-compact 1. Sample from main-cart: `<img src="...fixture.png?width=320" srcset=...`. In the browser, main-blog-single's featured-media div has that string as its textContent, and the div's min-content width of 345px is what breaks the 320px layout.
Consequence: On the cart page every line item shows a line of raw HTML where the product thumbnail should be. snippets/card-product.liquid:163 and snippets/cart-line-item.liquid:19 are shared snippets, so the blast radius is the cart, the cart drawer and any collection grid that reaches those code paths with a real image. The remaining 19 sites sit on branches that need a merchant-supplied image to reach, so they are latent rather than clear.
Recommended fix: Compute the alt text into a variable first — `{%- assign img_alt = img.alt | default: title | escape -%}` — then pass `alt: img_alt`. Apply to all 90 sites; the 23 escape-class sites first.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: A half-finished asset rename left 13 stylesheet and script references pointing at files that do not exist
Detail: The assets folder holds 89 code files; 67 are referenced by a Liquid file and 22 (146,467 bytes) are referenced by nothing. Separately, 13 asset_url references name files that are not in the folder. The two lists pair up, and the orphaned files' own header comments name the file the theme is asking for: assets/product-recently-viewed.js line 1 reads `// File: assets/section-product-recently-viewed.js` and the section requests exactly that name; assets/product-recommend.js line 1 reads `// File: assets/section-product-recommended.js`, likewise requested and likewise absent. account-main-order-tracking.js pairs with the requested account-main-account-order-tracking.js, and account-main-account.css with the requested account-main-account-login.css. This is one incomplete `section-` prefix rename, not 13 independent mistakes.
Evidence: p6/assets.json lists both sides. Missing: account-main-account-login.css, account-main-account-order-tracking.js, account-main-account-register.js, cart-drawer.js, global.js, predictive-search.css, q-base.css, section-product-recently-viewed.css, section-product-recently-viewed.js, section-product-recommended.js, section-product-reviews.css, social-media.css, transparent-hero-banner.css. Note that cart-drawer.js, global.js and q-base.css are requested by layout/theme.liquid, so those three 404 on every page of the store.
Consequence: Sections that ship with no working code: product-recently-viewed (both its CSS and JS 404), product-recommend (JS 404), call-to-action-web3, product-bundles, main-collection-classic and interactive-content-helper-predictive-search (each has a matching asset sitting unreferenced in the folder and loads nothing), call-to-action-featured-product (CSS loads, JS does not). Three 404s fire on every page load from theme.liquid. Shopify will still publish the theme; the failures are silent in the editor and visible only in the browser network tab.
Recommended fix: Rename the 22 orphans to the names the Liquid asks for, or change the 13 references to the names on disk — one decision per pair, checked against the header comment in each orphan. Then re-run an asset cross-reference before release.
Phase 3 notes: Missing reference repair is complete; dormant/orphan assets remain deliberately retained under the RC-13 restriction.

Finding: The collection filter checkboxes render zero pixels wide and cannot be seen or clicked
Detail: main-collection-classic marks up its facet filters as a native checkbox inside a flex `<label class="main-collection-classic__filter-option">`, with the intent that the checkbox appears beside its label text. The only rule the section writes for it is `margin-top: 2px`. The global input rule (P6-01) gives the checkbox `width: 100%`, and the label sets the item to `flex: 0 0 auto`, so a percentage width against a shrink-to-fit flex basis resolves to zero. The section's own stylesheet, assets/main-collection-classic.css, is one of the 22 orphaned files (P6-09), so in a real store it does not load at all and even the `margin-top` rule is absent.
Evidence: Rendered at 1440px: seven filter checkboxes, each measuring 0 x 44 CSS pixels, computed width 0px, flex `0 0 auto`, inside a 26px-wide label. getBoundingClientRect width is 0, so the control has no hit area. The sibling section main-collection-simple uses `flex: 0 1 auto` on the same construction and gets the opposite failure — checkboxes 176 to 195 pixels wide inside a 294px row.
Consequence: On the classic collection template a shopper sees filter labels with no checkbox next to them and cannot tick one. Filtering is the primary way a shopper narrows a large catalogue, so this is a direct conversion problem, not a cosmetic one. It is also invisible in the theme editor, where a merchant sees the filter list and reasonably assumes it works.
Recommended fix: Fixing P6-01 fixes this. In the meantime `.main-collection-classic__filter-option input { width: auto; min-height: 0; flex: none; }` restores it, and the same rule with `flex: none` fixes main-collection-simple's 195px checkboxes. Restore assets/main-collection-classic.css as part of P6-09 or the section ships unstyled regardless.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: Social links can never render in either footer
Detail: Both footers gate every social row on settings.social_facebook_link, social_instagram_link, social_tiktok_link, social_youtube_link, social_pinterest_link and social_linkedin_link. None of those six settings exist in config/settings_schema.json, which defines social_url_facebook, social_url_instagram, social_url_tiktok, social_url_youtube, social_url_twitter and social_url_pinterest instead. The `!= blank` gate is therefore always false.
Evidence: 24 call sites (4 per network across the two files). Populating the schema-correct settings with real URLs and rendering both footers produced zero social anchor elements in the body; the only qf3__social-link text in the output is the CSS rule that styles links which never appear.
Consequence: A merchant fills in their social URLs in Theme settings and the footer stays empty with no indication why. footer-three's 'Social style' block control is unreachable as a direct result.
Recommended fix: Rename the six reads in footer-two and footer-three to the social_url_* ids, add a LinkedIn setting to the schema, and decide whether Twitter/X should be surfaced in the footers.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: Gradient overlay renders invalid CSS in the default configuration
Detail: The template writes rgba({{ colour | color_to_rgb }}, {{ opacity | divided_by: 100.0 }}). Shopify's color_to_rgb returns a complete rgb(r, g, b) string, not bare components, so the result nests one colour function inside another.
Evidence: Rendered output: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(rgb(0, 0, 0), 0.6), rgba(rgb(0, 0, 0), 0)) -- invalid CSS, silently not painted. 4 instances across the two sections (sub-banner-transparent lines 332 and 389; transparent-hero-banner x2).
Consequence: overlay_type defaults to 'gradient' in both sections, so the default overlay is broken out of the box. Text contrast over imagery depends on this overlay.
Recommended fix: Use color_modify: 'alpha' to build the colour, or interpolate the components rather than wrapping color_to_rgb output in rgba().
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: Slide ships pointing at https://example.com/video.mp4
Detail: The slide block's video_url setting carries that URL as its schema default. The media chain begins {% if b.video_url != blank %}, which is therefore permanently true for a freshly added section.
Evidence: Rendering a default slide produces a <video autoplay muted loop> element with <source src="https://example.com/video.mp4">.
Consequence: Two problems at once: the section renders a broken video on install, and the image and background-colour branches below it are unreachable until the merchant manually empties the field, which nothing in the editor signals.
Recommended fix: Remove the default from video_url. Placeholder content belongs in a preset, not in a schema default that changes which branch runs.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: The parent_slide defect strands twelve further settings
Detail: Already reported at section level. product and content_column blocks are matched to a slide with `where: 'settings.parent_slide', slide_id`, where slide_id is the slide block's internal Shopify id. A merchant has no way to know that value, so the match never succeeds.
Evidence: Newly quantified this pass. Unreachable as a direct consequence: extra_grid_cols, extra_grid_gap, product.parent_slide, product.show_price, product.show_button, product.button_text, content_column.parent_slide, content_column.icon, content_column.title, content_column.text -- plus the --q-cols and --q-gap tokens that feed the product grid, which are consumed correctly but never emitted.
Consequence: Two entire block types in this section are inert for every merchant. This single defect accounts for more dead controls than any other in the theme.
Recommended fix: Replace the typed id with a select populated from the slide blocks, or scope the child blocks under their slide instead of matching by id.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: The badge block type is never rendered
Detail: The badge block is declared in the schema with badge_text and badge_icon, and the section carries CSS for it (.qcta__badges, .qcta__badge). No branch anywhere in the section renders a block of type 'badge'.
Evidence: Checked across all ten combinations of the two settings that govern layout (layout_variant x mode). A probe string placed in badge_text never appears in the output.
Consequence: The Web3 preset ships three badge blocks pre-filled with 'Non-custodial', 'Gas-optimized' and 'Secure'. A merchant installing that preset gets three badges in the editor that display nothing.
Recommended fix: Render the badge blocks in the web3 layout branch, where the CSS clearly expects them.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: Broken filter chain renders 'background: 0' in two places
Detail: Line 425 (block-level content panel) writes: background: {{ panel_color | color_modify: 'alpha', panel_opacity | divided_by: 100.0 }}. Liquid applies filters left to right across the whole chain and cannot nest a filter inside another filter's argument, so divided_by: 100.0 is applied to the OUTPUT of color_modify -- a colour string -- rather than to panel_opacity. Line 159 makes the identical mistake at section level with content_overlay_color and content_overlay_opacity.
Evidence: Rendered at three colours and three opacities; every combination produced the literal `background: 0;`. backdrop-filter, border-radius and padding on the same element still work, which is exactly why only the colour and opacity controls measured dead.
Consequence: The content panel and the section content overlay both render with no background whatsoever. Four merchant controls (panel colour, panel opacity, overlay colour, overlay opacity) do nothing. The section-level pair also means this slipped past section-level testing.
Recommended fix: Compute the alpha into a variable first: {%- assign a = panel_opacity | divided_by: 100.0 -%} then color_modify: 'alpha', a.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: Missing snippet rendered from the layout — superseded by P5-01
Detail: Originally reported as a missing file. The file exists as snippets/utilities.liquid; the layout renders 'utilities.css', a rename that was never followed through. Evidence: Theme-wide scan of every render/include target against snippets/ on disk. Confirmed absent from both snippets/ and assets/.
Consequence: Site-wide fatal render error. Also a category error: a stylesheet is being pulled in as a snippet.
Recommended fix: See P5-01. Change the call to {% render 'utilities' %}.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: All three product-page presets install an empty layout
Detail: The section is a theme-block container. Its three presets -- 'Standard product', 'Conversion product' and 'Story product' -- each build product-layout-row > product-layout-column and stop there. No content block is nested inside any column, even though blocks/product-layout-column.liquid renders {% content_for 'blocks' %} and exists to hold them.
Evidence: Rendered all three presets: the row and column markup and their CSS custom properties emit correctly, `data-shopify-editor-block` attributes are present, and every column's inner div is empty -- 0 characters of visible text in all three. The sibling section block-section, built the same way, nests content-heading, content-rich-text, content-button, content-badge and content-icon-list in its columns and renders 268, 1551 and 1509 characters respectively.
Consequence: A merchant choosing any product-page preset gets a page with no gallery, title, price or add-to-cart -- structure and nothing else. That block-section next door does this correctly makes it an oversight rather than a deliberate blank canvas.
Recommended fix: Nest the product content blocks inside the columns of each preset, the way block-section's presets do. The block files already exist in blocks/.
Phase 3 notes: Existing three builder presets now contain admitted gallery/title/price/form/description blocks. Saved templates/settings_data were not rewritten.

Finding: 49 of the 61 content blocks cannot be placed on a normal page
Detail: The general content builder is block-section > layout-row > layout-column > content blocks. layout-column's schema names exactly 12 accepted block types (content-alert, badge, button, button-group, code, divider, heading, icon, icon-list, quote, rich-text, spacer) and does not declare {"type": "@theme"}. The theme ships 61 content-* blocks, so 49 of them -- content-testimonials, content-logo-cloud, content-newsletter, content-marquee, content-timeline, content-accordion, content-featured-product, content-product-grid, content-tabs, content-stats-counter and the rest -- can never be added to a page built with block-section.
Evidence: Compared layout-column's accepted types against blocks/ on disk. The only container in the theme that accepts everything is product-layout-column, which declares @theme -- and that one lives inside product-block-section, i.e. product templates. All 102 blocks render correctly standalone, so this is purely an availability gap, not a rendering fault.
Consequence: A merchant building a homepage or landing page with the block setter has 12 primitives available -- heading, text, button, divider, spacer and a few more -- while the marketing blocks the theme actually ships sit unreachable. Their only route is inside a product layout column on a product template, which is the wrong place for a testimonial wall or a logo cloud.
Recommended fix: Add {"type": "@theme"} to layout-column's blocks array, as product-layout-column already does, or name the missing content-* types explicitly.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: 13 referenced assets do not exist on disk
Detail: Files referenced through asset_url that are absent from assets/: account-main-account-login.css, account-main-account-order-tracking.js, account-main-account-register.js, cart-drawer.js, global.js, predictive-search.css, q-base.css, section-product-recently-viewed.css, section-product-recently-viewed.js, section-product-recommended.js, section-product-reviews.css, social-media.css, transparent-hero-banner.css.

Finding: The site-wide render error is a rename that was never followed through
Detail: Line 71 calls {% render 'utilities.css' %}. The file exists as snippets/utilities.liquid, and its own first line is a leftover comment reading 'snippets/utilities.css.liquid' -- the file was renamed and the reference was not. Shopify emits a Liquid error at that point rather than failing the page, so the effect is that the utilities stylesheet never loads anywhere.
Evidence: snippets/utilities.liquid is present and 1,237 bytes. It defines .container, .section-pad and the .h1-.h6 type scale. The .container class alone is used in 15 files.

Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: 73 image alt-text fallbacks never fire, so images ship with empty alt
Detail: The pattern `{{ media | image_url: width: 900 | image_tag: loading: 'lazy', alt: media.alt | default: 'Product image' }}` appears 73 times across 31 files. Liquid parses the chain as image_tag(...) then default(...), so the trailing filter binds to the string -- which is never empty -- and the alt fallback is discarded. 68 sites use | default:, 5 use | append:.
Evidence: Rendered directly with an empty alt source: output is . The | append: variant is the confirmed ' photo' text leak in call-to-action-reviews. Concentrated where product imagery lives: product-gallery (6), content-product-recommendations (6), content-product-carousel (4), content-product-grid (4).
Consequence: When a merchant has not typed alt text -- the common case -- the image renders alt="", which assistive technology treats as decorative and skips. WCAG 2.1 AA 1.1.1 failure on product and content imagery.
Recommended fix: Compute the alt into a variable first: {%- assign alt = media.alt | default: 'Product image' -%} then alt: alt.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: The section renders white text on a transparent background, out of the box
Detail: The section's CSS falls back to `background: var(--q-powered-bg, var(--q-section-bg, transparent))` and `color: var(--q-powered-muted, var(--q-section-muted, rgba(255,255,255,.72)))`. --q-powered-* is only defined when use_custom_colors is on, and that defaults to false. --q-section-muted is set by no file in the theme and --q-section-bg only by three unrelated sections. So the fallbacks apply: no background, white text.
Evidence: Rendered and measured: 11 text nodes at a contrast ratio of 1.00 against their effective background, every ancestor transparent, no image or painted element behind them.
Consequence: A merchant adds the section and sees nothing. WCAG 1.4.3 failure at the most extreme possible ratio.
Recommended fix: Give the section real default colours rather than dark-theme fallbacks, or implement the .q-section--bg-* system described in P5-04.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: Kicker letter-spacing is applied 100x too wide because the divide-by-100 the label promises is missing
Detail: Line 131 emits `--q-bhs-kicker-ls: {{ section.settings.kicker_ls }}em;`. The setting's own label is "Kicker letter spacing (x100)" and its default is 8, i.e. the author's intent is 0.08em. There is no `| divided_by: 100` on this line. The sibling section featured-content-sale-highlight declares the same setting with the same label and does divide (`| divided_by: 100.0`), and featured-content-testimonial-highlight uses `| times: 0.01`.
Evidence: Rendered at 1440px with theme defaults: computed letter-spacing on the kicker is 96px at a 12px font size. The correctly-written sibling featured-content-sale-highlight measures 1.04px on the same element class. The section also overflows the viewport horizontally at 320px and 375px, which is how it was found.
Consequence: The kicker reads as single letters spread across the full width of the screen out of the box, and causes horizontal scroll on phones. No merchant setting can fix it: the range is 0-20 step 1, so the smallest non-zero value is 1em.
Recommended fix: Append `| divided_by: 100.0` to line 131, matching featured-content-sale-highlight.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: Kicker letter-spacing default of 6 is emitted as 6em, spreading the kicker to 479px
Detail: Line 133 emits `letter-spacing: {{ s.kicker_letter_spacing }}em;`. The schema declares `{"type":"range","id":"kicker_letter_spacing","label":"Kicker letter spacing (em)","min":0,"max":20,"step":1,"default":6}`. Unlike the six sibling sections that carry the same control, this one has no ×100 scaling anywhere — but it kept the ×100-style default of 6.
Evidence: Rendered at 1440px: computed letter-spacing 72px at a 12px font size. At a 320px viewport the string "Bundle & Save" measures 479px in a 270px box, producing document scrollWidth 504 against a 320px viewport. Same failure at 375px.
Consequence: Out of the box the section's kicker is unreadable and the section scrolls sideways on phones. The three sibling controls on the same section (heading_letter_spacing, subheading_letter_spacing, description_letter_spacing) share the fault but default to 0, so they are latent: any merchant who moves those sliders one notch gets 1em.
Recommended fix: Either divide all four by 100 and keep the integer ranges, or change the ranges to min 0 / max 0.2 / step 0.01 and reset the kicker default to 0.06.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: Three sections overflow the viewport because grid tracks default to auto min sizing
Detail: A CSS grid track's implicit minimum is `auto`, so a track cannot shrink below its item's min-content width unless it is written `minmax(0, 1fr)` or the item is given `min-width:0`. Three sections hit this. form-waitlist: `.q-field { min-width: 240px }` and the inline variant's `min-width: 220px` give the card a min-content of 489px, so the single grid track computes to 488.8px inside a 272px container. account-main-account-dashboard: the recent-orders table has `white-space: nowrap` on every th/td and no scroll wrapper, giving a min-content of 341px inside a 296px container. sub-banner-web3: the section is `display:grid` and `.qsbw3__stage` carries `margin-inline: clamp(16px, 4vw, 56px)`, so the auto track sizes to the stage's min-content plus both margins (358.4px at a 320px viewport).
Evidence: Measured with computed styles at the failing viewports. form-waitlist at 320: parent .q-grid width 272px, grid-template-columns resolves to 488.812px. account-main-account-dashboard at 320: parent 296px, track 341.312px. sub-banner-web3 at 320/375/768/1024: section 320px, track 358.391px; the stage renders 326px wide starting at x=16.
Consequence: Horizontal scroll on phones for the waitlist form and the customer dashboard, and on tablets as well for sub-banner-web3. account-main-account-dashboard is notable because the sibling section account-main-account-orders wraps the same table in `.qtmAccountOrders__tableWrap { overflow-x: auto }` — the dashboard copy of the table lost the wrapper.
Recommended fix: Write the tracks as `minmax(0, 1fr)`; change `.q-field { min-width: 240px }` to `min-width: min(240px, 100%)`; wrap the dashboard's orders table in an `overflow-x:auto` container as account-main-account-orders already does.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: The slideshow's controller script and stylesheet are loaded by nothing and the markup it drives does not exist
Detail: section-slideshow.js binds three hooks — [data-q-carousel-dot], [data-q-carousel-toggle] and [data-q-progress] — and none of the three appears anywhere in the theme's rendered markup or in any Liquid source. The script is also referenced by no asset_url call, and neither is section-slideshow.css. Both sit in the folder unused.
Evidence: 265 distinct selectors were extracted from the 36 JavaScript files and cross-referenced against the ids, classes and data-attributes present in the rendered output of every section and block (818 ids, 4,429 classes, 786 data-attributes). 19 selectors resolved to nothing; 15 of those match markup the script itself creates at runtime (quick-view, wishlist, collection-modern filters) and were excluded. These three are the residue: no source emits them and no script creates them.
Consequence: The slideshow-banner section renders its own dots inline (measured as button.q-dot 10x10) rather than through this controller, so nothing is broken on screen — but 15.7KB of maintained code is dead, and anyone reading section-slideshow.js will reasonably assume it is live.
Recommended fix: Decide whether slideshow-banner should be migrated onto this controller or the pair should be deleted. Do not leave it as-is; this is the file most likely to be edited by mistake.
Phase 3 notes: Excluded broad dormant-code/CSS work; no deletion or architecture rewrite.

Finding: An entire collection template is present in the theme but wired to nothing
Detail: section-collection-modern.js (14,890 bytes), section-collection-modern.css (7,835) and section-collection-modern-simple.css (12,846) are all orphaned, and there is no host section that loads them. Ten snippets in the same cluster are likewise reachable from no section. Total dead weight is roughly 64KB.
Evidence: Asset cross-reference plus the snippet reachability graph from Document 12. The JS's five unresolved hooks ([data-qcm-open-filters], [data-qcm-close-filters], [data-qcm-compareclear], [data-qcm-comparego], [data-qcm-qv-close]) are all created by the script itself, which is consistent with a complete but unmounted feature rather than a broken one.
Consequence: The theme carries a finished collection experience that a merchant cannot reach. It is either an unfinished feature that should ship, or leftovers that should be removed — both are defensible, but shipping it in this state means 64KB of unreviewed code in the store and a confusing folder for whoever maintains it next.
Recommended fix: Decide: build the host section and the snippet wiring, or delete the cluster. This is a product decision, not a bug fix, and it should be made before launch rather than after.
Phase 3 notes: Excluded broad dormant-code/CSS work; no deletion or architecture rewrite.

Finding: slide.animation is read by nothing
Detail: The schema declares animation as a select labelled 'Content anim.'. The string slide.settings.animation appears nowhere in the section, in either of the two snippets it renders (multipurpose-banner-slide, multipurpose-banner-content), or in assets/multipurpose-hero-banner.css.
Evidence: Survived every configuration tried, and a source search of the complete render tree returns no read. The only 'animation' in the section CSS is an unrelated prefers-reduced-motion reset.
Consequence: A merchant-visible control that does nothing.
Recommended fix: Wire it to a class on the content wrapper, or remove it.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: button.size is read zero times
Detail: The button block declares size as a select (sm / md / lg, default md). The string settings.size does not appear anywhere in the section.
Evidence: Confirmed across all five layout variants with the block's own gates both open and closed: no configuration produced any change. Source search returns 0 reads.
Consequence: A merchant-visible control that does nothing. The button markup has no size class at all, so buttons cannot be sized.
Recommended fix: Append a size class to btn_class, or remove the setting.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: The literal text ' photo' leaks onto the page beside every reviewer avatar
Detail: Line 512 writes alt: b.reviewer_name | append: ' photo' inside image_tag's argument list. Liquid does not allow a pipe inside a filter argument, so Shopify applies append to the whole image_tag output instead of to the alt text.
Evidence: Rendered output in the masonry layout: photo -- the word 'photo' is printed as page text, and the alt attribute loses its intended suffix.
Consequence: Visible stray text next to each reviewer avatar, plus a small accessibility regression in the alt text. Same fault class as the nine sites already documented in Document 3 and as P2-09; three instances found this pass, so this is a recurring authoring pattern rather than a one-off.
Recommended fix: Assign the alt text before the filter chain: {%- assign avatar_alt = b.reviewer_name | append: ' photo' -%} then alt: avatar_alt.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: The screen-reader label control is never read; aria-label falls back to visible text
Detail: The block declares sr_label, labelled 'Screen reader label (optional)' with the default 'View post on social media'. Line 355 builds the accessible name from b.link_label instead: `assign sr_base = b.link_label | default: 'View post'`. b.sr_label is read nowhere in the section or any snippet (0 occurrences outside the schema).
Evidence: Measured inert, then confirmed by source search of the full render tree and by reading the aria-label construction at lines 355-369.
Consequence: An accessibility control that does nothing. Whatever the merchant writes for screen-reader users is silently discarded, and the aria-label duplicates the visible link text rather than describing the destination -- the opposite of what the control exists for.
Recommended fix: assign sr_base = b.sr_label | default: b.link_label | default: 'View post'
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: The Highlight text feature emits a span that no CSS styles
Detail: When highlight_text matches a substring of the heading, the block wraps that substring in <span class="qtm-heading__highlight">. The class qtm-heading__highlight appears in exactly one place in the theme -- the line in blocks/content-heading.liquid that writes it. No stylesheet, snippet or section defines a rule for it.
Evidence: Rendered content-heading with highlight_text set to a word present in the default heading: the span is emitted, so the substitution works. A theme-wide search for the class finds no CSS rule. The highlighted word therefore renders identically to the text around it.
Consequence: A merchant uses 'Highlight text' expecting emphasis and sees no change. It is the same root cause as P4-02 -- markup written for CSS that does not exist -- on the block most likely to be used.
Recommended fix: Add a rule for .qtm-heading__highlight in whichever stylesheet ends up carrying the primitive block styles.
Phase 3 notes: Current qtm-content-blocks-engine.js includes qtm-heading__highlight consumers. Existing source contradicts the missing-style diagnosis.

Finding: A section-surface design system is referenced but was never built
Detail: 15 sections emit a class of the form q-section--bg-{{ style }} and rely on the companion properties --q-section-bg, --q-section-fg, --q-section-muted and --q-section-card-bg. No file in the theme defines any .q-section--bg-* rule. --q-section-fg, --q-section-muted and --q-section-card-bg are set by zero files; --q-section-bg is set by three sections for their own use only.
Evidence: Theme-wide search across sections, snippets, blocks and assets. The 'Background style' select on each of these sections therefore has no effect.
Consequence: Fourteen of the fifteen still render legibly because their text colours resolve to something readable; 3rd-party-powered-by does not (P5-03). The wider cost is that a documented, merchant-facing control does nothing on 15 sections. Same root cause as the unstyled primitive blocks in Document 11: markup and tokens written for CSS that does not exist.
Recommended fix: Implement the .q-section--bg-* rules and define the section-surface properties globally, or remove the class and the Background style control.
Phase 3 notes: Shared q-section--bg-* contract now covers 13 retained consumers; the original 15-section count predates removals.

Finding: 78% of the theme's CSS is embedded in Liquid and re-sent on every page load
Detail: 232 <style> blocks and 11 {% stylesheet %} blocks inside section, snippet and block files hold 1,880,500 bytes of CSS, against 517,964 bytes in assets/*.css. There are also 684 inline style attributes and 334,764 bytes of inline JavaScript.
Evidence: Measured on a representative eight-section homepage: 157,006 bytes of body HTML, of which 107,392 bytes -- 68% -- is CSS inside <style> blocks. Per section: header-two 23KB of CSS, footer-two 20KB, featured-content-collection-spotlight 18KB, hero-banner 13KB.
Consequence: None of it can be browser-cached, it is re-sent on every page view, it is duplicated when a section appears twice on a page, and it bypasses Shopify's asset minification. This is the largest single lever on the theme's page weight.
Recommended fix: Move the static majority of each section's CSS into assets/*.css loaded once, and keep only the genuinely dynamic custom-property declarations inline. The token pattern the theme already uses makes this a mechanical split rather than a rewrite.
Phase 3 notes: Excluded broad dormant-code/CSS work; no deletion or architecture rewrite.

Finding: Accessibility: 58 contrast failures, 11 unlabelled fields, 17 anchors without href
Detail: Audited on rendered output at 1440px with the theme's stylesheets loaded, measuring computed colour against the effective background and checking for anything painted behind the text before calling a failure.
Evidence: 58 genuine contrast failures across 26 sections (WCAG 1.4.3), led by 3rd-party-powered-by (11), grid-banner (6), footer-five (5), footer-four (4), footer-two (4). 39 images render with an empty alt attribute and 101 without width/height (layout shift). 11 form fields have no associated label -- 5 further ones are deliberate honeypots and were excluded -- including the whole of 3rd-party-bulk-ordering's form and the variant and quantity selectors on main-product-compact and main-product-modern-variant (WCAG 3.3.2, 4.1.2). 17 anchors render without an href, and 6 controls have no accessible name. 3 sections skip a heading level, h1 straight to h3 (WCAG 1.3.1). 25 target="_blank" links across 2 files omit rel="noopener".
Consequence: These are the failures that survived a deliberate false-positive filter; a further 61 flagged items were text over imagery or a painted element and are excluded rather than reported.
Recommended fix: Work the accompanying CSV in order: labels on the bulk-ordering and product forms first, then the contrast list, then width/height on images.
Phase 3 notes: Shared focus, form input geometry, drawer focus and section surface foundations repaired. Original section-specific labeling/contrast/link cases are not all closed.

Finding: The orders table's scroll wrapper is switched off at exactly the width where it is needed
Detail: assets/account-main-account-orders.css:176 gives `.qtmAccountOrders__tableWrap` `width:100%; overflow-x:auto`, which is correct. Inside the narrow-viewport media query, line 521 sets `[id^="QtmAccountMainOrders-"].qtmAccountOrders--table .qtmAccountOrders__tableWrap { overflow: visible; }` — the shorthand resets overflow-x back to visible for the table layout variant, so the table escapes its container instead of scrolling inside it.
Evidence: At a 768px viewport the table measures 898.7px wide inside a 736px wrapper, right edge 916, document scrollWidth exceeds the viewport. account-main-account-order shows the same class of failure at 320px: `.qtmAccountOrder__main` and `.qtmAccountOrder__aside` both render 351px wide at x=12 in a 320px viewport.
Consequence: The order history page scrolls sideways on tablets and small laptops in the `--table` layout. The `--hybrid` variant is unaffected because it hides the wrapper and shows cards instead.
Recommended fix: Change line 521 to `overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: visible`, or drop the rule — the intent appears to have been vertical overflow only.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: 199 interactive targets are smaller than 24x24 CSS pixels at phone widths
Detail: Measured at a 390px viewport across all 159 sections, with the WCAG inline exception applied (links sitting inside a sentence of running text are excluded). Four groups remain. (A) 24 carousel and slider controls with both axes under 24px: q-dot 8x8 on call-to-action-featured-product and slideshow-banner, q-hero-dot 10x10 on hero-banner and sub-banner-classic, q-review-dot 10-12px on call-to-action-reviews, q-carousel-dot 12-14px on carousel-hero-banner, q-dev-pin 14x14 on maps-store-locator, qcmQv__arrow 6x26 on collection-modern-quick-view. (B) 158 navigation links whose height is 16-23px while the width is fine — 81 of them in the five footer sections (footer-five 24, footer-two 17, footer-one 15, footer-three 13, footer-four 12), the rest in the account nav, the blog sidebar and product-card title links. (C) 12 checkbox/radio inputs, chiefly product-bundles' qtm-include at 18x44. (D) 5 disclosure summaries at 18px tall.
Evidence: p6/tap2.json holds every element with its class, computed display and measured box. The raw sweep found 197 candidates at 320px; after adding the inline exception and re-measuring at 390px the figure is 199 across 37 sections, so the exception removed almost nothing — these are list items and standalone controls, not inline prose links.
Consequence: Group A is the practical problem: 8-14px carousel dots are close to impossible to hit reliably on a phone and there is no other way to jump between slides. Group B is a bulk WCAG 2.5.8 failure that a compliance audit will flag on every page, since the footer is global.
Recommended fix: Group A: keep the visual dot size and add `padding: 8px; background-clip: content-box;` or a `::before` hit area of at least 24x24. Group B: add `padding-block: 4px` to the footer, account-nav and sidebar link rules — one line per list, five of the twelve rules cover 81 of the 158.
Phase 3 notes: Common keyboard controls repaired; no claim that all 199 component targets have been resized.

Finding: The popup's manual open trigger can never fire because no file emits the attribute it listens for
Detail: global-popup.js attaches its open handler to [data-qtm-popup-open]. That attribute appears in no Liquid file and in no rendered output, and no script writes it at runtime.
Evidence: Same 265-selector cross-reference as P6-10. [data-qtm-popup-open] is the only unresolved selector in this file, and unlike the quick-view and wishlist cases the script does not create it.
Consequence: The popup's scroll-depth and exit-intent triggers still work, so the feature appears functional. The manual trigger — a merchant putting a button in a rich-text block to open the popup — silently does nothing, and there is no documentation telling a merchant what attribute to use.
Recommended fix: Either emit the attribute from a documented block, or remove the handler and document the two triggers that do work.
Phase 3 notes: Excluded broad dormant-code/CSS work; no deletion or architecture rewrite.

Finding: promo_block.link_label can never be used
Detail: snippets/header-marketplace-departments.liquid reads link_label only as a fallback when button_label is blank, but button_label ships with the default 'Explore now', so it is never blank and the fallback never fires.
Evidence: Survived 511 section configurations in the pairwise verifier. link_url was correctly NOT flagged, because button_url has no default and that fallback genuinely can fire.
Consequence: The control is labelled 'Legacy link label' in the schema, which suggests it is a leftover. It occupies editor space and does nothing.
Recommended fix: Remove the setting, or drop button_label's default so the fallback is reachable.
Phase 3 notes: Legacy label remains the fallback only when button_label is blank. No repair/closure claimed; retained for a focused dependency decision.

Finding: The Categories block's 'Show count' checkbox is read by nothing
Detail: The tags block declares show_count ('Show count', default false). The id appears exactly once in the file -- in the schema at line 845 -- and nowhere in the section body or in blog-card, the only snippet the section renders.
Evidence: Measured inert, then confirmed by source: 1 occurrence in the file, all of it schema; 0 reads in the render tree.
Consequence: A merchant ticking 'Show count' on the Categories block sees no change. Post counts never appear.
Recommended fix: Render the count beside each tag when the setting is on, or remove the control.
Phase 3 notes: Show count still has no renderer. Accurate tag counts must not be inferred from a limited blog.articles page; requires a separately verified implementation.

Finding: The reward tier's 'Reward type' select is read by nothing
Detail: The reward_tier block declares reward_type (select, default 'shipping'). The id appears exactly once in main-cart.liquid -- in the schema -- and is read by none of the five snippets the section renders (cart-addons, cart-line-item, cart-progress-rewards, cart-rewards-progress-bar, cart-summary).
Evidence: Measured inert, then confirmed by source: 1 occurrence in the section, all schema; the cart snippets read only threshold_amount, locked_text, unlocked_text and icon.
Consequence: A merchant choosing a reward type sees no difference. Every tier behaves the same regardless of the选 selection.
Recommended fix: Branch on reward_type when rendering the tier, or remove the control.
Phase 3 notes: See root-cause implementation map and grouped commits. Shopify rendering remains unverified.

Finding: 27 of 86 snippets are rendered by nothing
Detail: 18% of the snippet layer, 61,890 bytes, has no caller anywhere in sections, snippets, blocks, layout or templates. The largest group is a complete modern collection UI -- collection-modern-toolbar, -product-card, -facets, -sort, -pagination, -active-filters, -compare-tray, -empty-state and two utils files, 10 snippets and 28,265 bytes -- for which no main-collection-modern section exists. header-two-mega-menu (10,259 bytes) is superseded by an inline mega menu in header-two, which renders no snippets at all. cart-drawer, search-form-predictive and search-controller are orphaned alongside their own missing assets (cart-drawer.js, predictive-search.css).
Evidence: Full render-graph built from every render and include across the theme.
Consequence: Dead code rather than a defect. It inflates the theme, and it makes the collection-modern and cart-drawer features look available when nothing hosts them.
Recommended fix: Either wire the collection-modern set to a section and ship it, or delete the group. Same decision for the header-two and search clusters.
Phase 3 notes: Excluded broad dormant-code/CSS work; no deletion or architecture rewrite.

Finding: Countdown unit labels render at 9px at every viewport
Detail: assets/header-four.css:347 sets `.qtmHeaderFour__countdownUnit span { font-size: 9px; opacity: 0.7 }` for the Days / Hours / Min / Sec labels. There is no viewport at which this scales up. sub-banner-web3's kicker resolves to 10.4px at 320-375px and 10.8px at 768px.
Evidence: Measured at 320, 375, 768, 1024 and 1920: header-four's four labels are 9px at all five. Only these two sections in the theme place text under 11px.
Consequence: 9px at 70% opacity is below the practical readability floor and fails common brand accessibility checklists, though it is not a numbered WCAG failure on its own.
Recommended fix: Raise to 11px and drop the opacity to 0.85, or remove the labels and rely on the `d h m s` suffixes.
Phase 3 notes: No blanket type-size redesign. The component-specific small labels remain for later accessibility review.

Finding: Two scaffolding stubs ship as sections, with no schema and a setting that does not exist
Detail: sections/header.liquid and sections/footer.liquid are two lines each. Neither has a `{% schema %}` block, so neither can be added or configured in the theme editor, and both read `settings.shop_name`, which is not declared anywhere in config/settings_schema.json — the theme's 13 setting groups have no such id.
Evidence:
header.liquid is `

{{ settings.shop_name }}

`; footer.liquid is `

© {{ 'now' | date: '%Y' }} {{ settings.shop_name }}

`. Both were caught because the measurement harness could not load a schema for them. layout/theme.liquid renders header-one through header-five and footer-one through footer-five, so neither stub is reachable — they are unreferenced.
Consequence: No shopper impact today. The risk is that `header` and `footer` are the two most obvious names in the folder, so anyone new to the theme will open these first and conclude the header is two lines long. They also make the section count misleading: 159 files, 157 real sections.
Recommended fix: Delete both, or give them a schema and a real implementation if they were meant to be the fallback layout.
Phase 3 notes: Absent in the approved post-Phase-2 source; no Phase-3 deletion.
